Summary: Anxiety is a human experience the Bible takes seriously — and it offers something better than denial: a God who invites us to bring every worry to him. From Philippians 4 to the Psalms to Jesus' own words, Scripture gives anxious hearts practices, promises, and a Person to trust. This topical study is gentle and practical, for anyone whose mind will not quiet.
Steps: Read Philippians 4:6-7 and Matthew 6:25-34 together, noting what Jesus and Paul actually promise — and what they do not; Name your anxieties specifically, in writing: vague worry grows in the dark, and naming it is a first act of honesty; Practice the Philippians pattern daily: present each worry to God, with thanksgiving, and ask for his peace; Pray a psalm of trust (Psalm 23, 27, or 46) aloud when anxiety rises, letting its words steady you; Identify one practical step within your control for each worry — and one thing you must entrust to God; Talk with a trusted friend, pastor, or counselor about persistent anxiety; Scripture's wisdom includes wise counsel
Questions: What is the difference between concern that moves you to act and anxiety that paralyzes you?; Why does Jesus say not to worry about tomorrow — is that a command, a comfort, or both?; How does thanksgiving change anxiety, in your experience — and why would Paul pair them?; What does it mean to cast your cares on God — is it a one-time act, or a daily practice?; When does anxiety need more than a Bible study — prayer, community, rest, or professional help — and how do you know?
Application: Each evening this week, write down one worry and one thing you are thankful for, and hand the worry to God in prayer before you sleep.
